name: French Beige
lede: French Beige is a light-brown shade-name, one of a long run of "French" colors in the dictionaries, with no recorded story of its own.

sections.title: The name
sections.body: Paterson calls French beige a light brown, and beige itself a light brown or yellowish grey that sold well in fashion cloth [1][2]. He lists it with the browns, between Florentine brown and French yellow [3]. The book gives no origin for the "French" in this name [1].

sections.title: The French family
sections.body: The dictionary carries a whole row of French colors with very different meanings: French blue is a greeny-blue or sometimes a purplish blue, French grey a bluish grey, French green a yellowy green, and French pink a pale yellow [4]. French purple was a lichen dye of the 1850s that helped turn the word [[mauve]] from a dye into a color [4]. Beige, [[french-blue]] and [[french-grey]] are in our list [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #A67B5B measures lightness 55.1, chroma 27.1 and hue angle 62 degrees, a medium, warm brown more saturated than most beiges [5]. It sits close to [[tan]] and [[brown]] [5].
